dropped.claim: The timing objection is critical: the Berry merger closed April 30, 2025, contributing only two months to FY2025, yet revenue grew 10.0% to $15.0B, suggesting the underlying business performed better than a 1.1% CAGR implies. However, operating income declining from $1.5B to $1.0B and ROE at 4.4% represent genuine profitability deterioration that cannot be dismissed as solely integration-related. The company generates stable operating cash flow of $1.4B with explicit management guidance that the merger will significantly increase cash generation, but this remains forward-looking and unproven. With two months of integration captured, FY2026 results will be the true test of whether synergies materialize and margins recover. The capital inefficiency is concerning but may reflect merger accounting effects. Until we see a full year of combined operations and evidence that the $1.5B FY2023 operating income level was not just a peak, this warrants monitoring rather than immediate deeper diligence or a pass.
